definition: Documenting Hate is a project of ProPublica, in collaboration with a number of journalistic, academic, and computing organizations, for systematic tracking of hate crimes and bias incidents.
details: It uses an online form to facilitate reporting of incidents by the general public. Since August 2017, it has also used machine learning and natural language processing techniques to monitor and collect news stories about hate crimes and bias incidents. As of October 2017, over 100 news organizations had joined the project.

explainer.lead: Documenting Hate is a ProPublica-led project that gathers reports and news coverage of hate crimes and bias incidents in one systematic effort. It matters because scattered individual accounts and local stories are hard to follow across many communities and news organizations.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a class trying to keep track of every time someone is treated badly because of who they are. One notebook collects what people report, while another collects related newspaper stories. Documenting Hate works like those notebooks, using an online form and computer tools to help journalists follow these incidents.
tiers.practitioner: The project combines structured submissions from a public online form with machine learning and natural language processing to monitor and collect relevant news stories, an approach it has used since August 2017.
tiers.paperLevel: Documenting Hate can be described as a systematic collection process D = R ∪ N, where R represents incidents reported through the public form and N represents news stories about hate crimes and bias incidents collected using machine learning and natural language processing. It is a ProPublica project conducted with journalistic, academic, and computing organizations.

explainer.example: A person reports a bias incident through the online form, while the project’s news-monitoring process separately collects a local news story about a hate crime. Both become part of the same broader effort to track incidents that might otherwise remain isolated.

explainer.intuition: Reports about hate and bias are spread across individual experiences and many news outlets. Documenting Hate brings those accounts into a shared tracking effort, using both public submissions and automated news monitoring.
howItWorks: A member of the public submits an incident through the online form.
The project gathers these public reports as part of its tracking work.
Machine learning and natural language processing monitor news stories for relevant coverage.
Collected reports and stories support systematic tracking by ProPublica and its collaborators.
explainer.whyItMatters: Combining public reports with news coverage makes it easier to follow hate crimes and bias incidents systematically. The participation of over 100 news organizations by October 2017 also gave the project a broad journalistic network.
misconceptions: It is not solely a machine-learning system; public reporting and journalistic collaboration are central.
It tracks both hate crimes and bias incidents, not only one category.
It is a ProPublica project with collaborators, not a single newsroom working alone.
